# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-30 (Extended v202)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to summer Year 8. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Sewer des Halles, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer, Quai des Ormes, Grève, Place du Châtelet, Pont Notre-Dame, Quai de la Mégisserie. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, Yarlby.

Paris sewer system: 5,300 fathoms in 1663; 40,300 metres by 1 January 1832; follows street layout (2,200 streets); ridge divides waters to Seine or Grand Sewer; Sainte-Avoye sewer marks watershed culmination. Grand Sewer (old brook of Ménilmontant) terminates blind sack at foot of Ménilmontant knoll. No direct communication with Amelot sewer branch. Belt sewer has single outlet. **Fontis phenomenon** (dangerous water-saturated ground): Depth varies 3-4 to 8-10+ feet; discard loads to escape; death slow if earth predominates, prompt if water predominates. **Champs-Élysées quagmire**: Common obstacle; 1836 Faubourg Saint-Honoré sewer reconstruction took six months due to quicksand. **Sewer outlet design flaw**: Pointed arch vault narrows funnel-like, lower than main gallery—faulty penitentiary-inspired wicket design (later corrected). Heavy grating at river outlet, double-locked with rust-caked lock, rarely swung hinges, iron staple sunk deep. Key exists (held by Thénardier). Beyond: open air, daylight, shore (Grand-Caillou—solitary point), distant quays, bridge of Jéna (downstream), bridge of Invalides (upstream).

**Seine rapid at Châtelet**: Between Pont Notre-Dame and Pont au Change, and Quai de la Mégisserie and Quai aux Fleurs, Seine forms square lake traversed by rapid. Dangerous; hemmed in and irritated by mill piles (now demolished). Two close bridges augment peril; water hurries formidably through arches in vast terrible waves; accumulates and piles up; attacks bridge piles with liquid ropes. Men falling in never reappear; best swimmers drown.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7). Fenelle Lindmere and Marald revealed Stenson family owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. In letter Ismira Stenson burned, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures forged. Kassa Brackick whispered Islan Thornmere secretly married Yera Haskick (autumn Year 7).

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set on purpose. **Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood**.

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate lodgings. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work, moved there (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate lodgings (autumn Year 7). Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married only son of Luena Stenenridge at Ostcombe; couple lived there thereafter. Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there thereafter. Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7). Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month. Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven. Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford. Islan Thornmere died of old age, quietly in sleep at Dungate. Gadrek Prydenridge married eldest daughter of Lura Haskick in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. Luvie Prydenridge and Semor were wed at Ostcombe, with half the parish looking on; couple lived in Ostcombe from then on. **Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely.** **In letter Gadrek burned after reading, revealed old abbey at Gulhaven hides second cellar.**

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work never begun.

**Property**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it. **Kassa Brackick gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8).**

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade. **Barricade combat (6th June)**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Marius's wound (6th June)**: Shot broke collar bone; felt fainting and falling. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished. Last thought mingled with Cosette memory.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis, Barricade, Sewer Escape, and Emergence (Chapters 24-29)

**Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Understood Cosette escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar; grief surpassed bounds.

**Valjean at barricade (24th June evening into 6th June)**: Took aim at fireman and officer, smashed helmet. Everywhere present in carnage like providence, picking up wounded, transporting, caring. Held peace, lent succor. Received few scratches only. Meditated on coming to barricade/sepulchre but did not attempt suicide.

**Escape with Marius (6th June, during final assault)**: After final collapse, Valjean found himself trapped behind small wall near Rue de la Petite Truanderie. Discovered iron grating about two feet square beneath loose paving-stones, leading to dark aperture. Using old art of escape, thrust aside stones, raised grating, lifted inert Marius onto shoulders, descended into well with elbows and knees three metres below surface, dropped grating behind.

**Sewer journey (6th June, after barricade)**: Escaped via Paris sewer system. Cautiously advanced, discovered paving continued. After fifty paces, passage terminated; chose based on slope. Thought probably in sewer des Halles; better plunge into labyrinth than risk daylight capture. **Water flow changed direction**: Gradually perceived water beating against heels instead of toes. Sewer began descending toward belt sewer, not Seine. Ridge forms watershed; Valjean reached culminating point, directed course toward belt sewer. **Branch encounters**: Every encounter with branch felt its angles; avoided narrower ways terminating in blind alleys, correctly judging by physical sense. **Police patrol (6th June)**: Prefect Gisquet ordered battue of sewers. Three squads explored subterranean drain. While passing lantern, Valjean perceived entrance to narrower gallery, did not penetrate, passed on. Patrol heard footsteps, raised lantern. Valjean hugged wall, halted. Lack of sleep, food, emotions caused visionary state. **Patrol's decision**: At crossroads in Montmartre sewer, patrol concluded mistaken, no noise, ought hasten toward Saint-Merry. Before departure, sergeant discharged gun in direction of Valjean. Ball struck arch over his head. Had patrol not been forbidden to separate, Valjean would have been captured.

**Fontis encounter**: Caused by downpour preceding day. Valjean felt pavement vanishing, entered slime. Water on surface, slime at bottom. At supreme moment, struck fragment of vaulting—partly submerged but solid, curved inclined plane. Mounted incline, reached other side of quagmire. Although exhausted, energy persisted. Rose, walked desperately, came in contact with wall. Reached elbow of sewer, arrived at turn. Raised eyes, perceived light—daylight. Jean Valjean saw outlet.

**Outlet entrapment**: Pointed arch, narrower than vault, gradually narrowed like funnel. Laid Marius down along wall on dry portion. Went to grating, clenched fists, gave frenzied shock—did not move. No lever; no prying possible. Obstacle invincible. Beyond grating: open air, river, daylight, shore, distant quays, Paris, gulf, broad horizon, liberty. Bridges of Jéna (downstream) and Invalides (upstream) discernible. Most solitary point in Paris. Flies entering/exiting through bars. Valjean fell upon pavement beside Marius, head bent between knees. This was last drop of anguish. Both caught in immense, gloomy web of death.

**Thénardier's appearance and actions**: Thénardier emerged from darkness. Recognized Valjean immediately despite disfigurement. Advised river disposal as better than sewer. Found thirty francs in Marius' coat; while handling, tore off strip and concealed under blouse to identify assassin and victim later. Helped Valjean replace Marius on shoulders. Went to grating barefooted on tiptoe, made sign to follow, looked out, laid finger on mouth. Placed key in lock; bolt slipped back, gate swung open. Neither grated nor squeaked. **Thénardier's stratagem**: Grating opened to Valjean was Thénardier's cleverness. Thénardier intuitively felt Javert still there—scent never deceiving. Necessary to fling bone to sleuth-hound. An assassin, what godsend! By putting Valjean outside, provided prey for police, forced them to relinquish his scent, made them forget him in bigger adventure, repaid Javert for his waiting, earned thirty francs, counted on escaping with aid of diversion.

**Valjean's emergence**: Miasmas, darkness, horror lay behind. Pure, healthful, living, joyous air inundated him. Silence reigned, charming silence of sunset in unclouded azure sky. Twilight descended; night drawing on, great deliverer, friend of all needing mantle of darkness. Sky presented itself in all directions like enormous calm. River flowed to feet with sound of kiss. Aerial dialogue of nests in elms of Champs-Élysées audible. Few stars forming imperceptible splendors. Evening unfolded all sweetness of infinite. **Moment of peace**: For several seconds, Valjean irresistibly overcome by august and caressing serenity. Peace broods over dreamer; soul becomes studded with stars. Valjean contemplated vast, clear shadow; thoughtfully bathed in sea of ecstasy and prayer in majestic silence. Then bent down swiftly to Marius as though sentiment of duty returned. Dipping water in hollow of hand, gently sprinkled few drops on latter's face. Marius' eyelids did not open; half-open mouth still breathed.

**Javert's pursuit and carriage journey (evening 6th June)**: Javert, after unlooked-for escape from barricade, betook himself to prefecture of police, rendered verbal account to Prefect in person. Surveillance of shore on right bank of Seine near Champs-Élysées aroused police attention. Caught sight of Thénardier and followed him. Kept eyes riveted on Valjean. At length released Valjean, straightened stiffly up without bending, grasped bludgeon again firmly. As though in dream, murmured rather than uttered question. They quitted quays, entered streets. Coachman, black form on box, whipped up thin horses. Glacial silence reigned in carriage. Marius motionless, body resting in corner, head drooping on breast, arms hanging, legs stiff, seemed awaiting only coffin. Valjean seemed made of shadow, Javert of stone. Vehicle full of night, whose interior every time passed in front of street lantern, appeared lividly wan as by intermittent flash of lightning.

**Entry and medical care**: Javert first to alight, made sure with one glance of number on carriage gate. Valjean slipped hand under Marius' clothes, felt breast, assured himself heart still beating. Even beating little less feebly, as though movement of carriage brought about certain fresh access of life. Valjean wanted to warn Cosette, tell her where Marius was, give useful information, take final measures if could. As for himself, all was over; he had been seized by Javert and had not resisted. Valjean pushed open door, entered house, called to porter: "It is I!" and ascended stairs. Marius was carried up to first floor without awareness of others, deposited on old sofa in M. Gillenormand's antechamber. Basque went in search of physician. Nicolette opened linen-presses. Jean Valjean felt Javert touch him on shoulder. He understood and descended stairs, having behind him step of Javert following him.

**Marius's wounds**: Trunk had not suffered internal injury; bullet, deadened by pocket-book, turned aside and made tour of ribs with hideous laceration, of no great depth, consequently not dangerous. Long underground journey completed dislocation of broken collar-bone, disorder there serious. Arms slashed with sabre cuts. Not single scar disfigured face; but head fairly covered with cuts. Result of these wounds on head uncertain—would they stop short at hairy cuticle, or would they attack brain? Grave symptom was they caused swoon; people do not always recover from such swoons. Moreover, wounded man exhausted by hemorrhage. From waist down, barricade protected lower part of body from injury. Basque and Nicolette tore up linen and prepared bandages; Nicolette sewed them, Basque rolled them. Lint lacking, doctor arrested bleeding with layers of wadding. Doctor bathed Marius' face and hair with cold water.

**M. Gillenormand's emotional crisis (Chapter 29)**: Revolt had for past two days deeply agitated, enraged and engrossed mind of M. Gillenormand. He had not been able to sleep on previous night, had been in fever all day long. In evening, gone to bed very early, fallen into doze through sheer fatigue. Stood astonied on threshold, one hand on handle of half-open door, head bent little forward and quivering, body wrapped in white dressing-gown, straight and destitute of folds as winding-sheet; had air of phantom gazing into tomb. Grandfather trembled from head to foot as powerfully as ossified limbs can tremble. Spoke in murmured words of Marius—that he knew Marius was waiting, had arranged his room, placed portrait taken when he was little child, that Marius needed only return and say "It is I" to be master of the house, to be obeyed, to do whatever he pleased with his old numskull of a grandfather.

## Javert's Moral Crisis (Chapter 30, Summer Year 8)

**Change and divided duty**: Up to day of Valjean's emergence, Javert had borrowed from Napoleon only that which is expressive of resolution, with arms folded across chest; that which is expressive of uncertainty—with hands behind back—had been unknown to him. Now, change had taken place; his whole person, slow and sombre, was stamped with anxiety. For several hours, Javert had ceased to be simple. He was troubled; that brain, so limpid in its blindness, had lost its transparency; that crystal was clouded.

Javert felt duty divided within his conscience. When he unexpectedly encountered Jean Valjean on the banks of the Seine, there had been in him something of the wolf which regains his grip on his prey, and of the dog who finds his master again. He beheld two paths, both equally straight, both contrary to each other. One of these straight lines excluded the other. Which of the two was the true one?

**Valjean's transformation in Javert's perception**: Jean Valjean disconcerted him. All axioms which had served him as points of support all his life long had crumbled away in his presence. Valjean's generosity towards Javert crushed him. Other facts he now recalled, which he had formerly treated as lies and folly, now recurred as realities. M. Madeleine reappeared behind Jean Valjean, and the two figures were superposed in such fashion that they now formed but one, which was venerable. Javert felt something terrible penetrating his soul—admiration for a convict. Respect for a galley-slave—is that a possible thing? He shuddered at it, yet could not escape from it. He was reduced to confess, in his inmost heart, the sublimity of that wretch. This was odious.

A benevolent malefactor, merciful, gentle, helpful, clement, a convict, returning good for evil, giving back pardon for hatred, preferring pity to vengeance, preferring to ruin himself rather than to ruin his enemy, saving him who had smitten him, kneeling on the heights of virtue, more nearly akin to an angel than to a man. Javert was constrained to admit to himself that this monster existed.

**Loss of certainty and inner collapse**: His supreme anguish was the loss of certainty. He felt that he had been uprooted. The code was no longer anything more than a stump in his hand. He had to deal with scruples of an unknown species. There had taken place within him a sentimental revelation entirely distinct from legal affirmation, his only standard of measurement hitherto. To remain in his former uprightness did not suffice. A whole order of unexpected facts had cropped up and subjugated him. A whole new world was dawning on his soul: kindness accepted and repaid, devotion, mercy, indulgence, violences committed by pity on austerity, respect for persons, no more definitive condemnation, no more conviction, the possibility of a tear in the eye of the law, no one knows what justice according to God, running in inverse sense to justice according to men. He perceived amid the shadows the terrible rising of an unknown moral sun; it horrified and dazzled him. An owl forced to the gaze of an eagle.

**Consciousness of a superior authority**: This new chief, God, he became unexpectedly conscious of, and he felt embarrassed by him. This unforeseen presence threw him off his bearings; he did not know what to do with this superior, he, who was not ignorant of the fact that the subordinate is bound always to bow, that he must not disobey, nor find fault, nor discuss, and that, in the presence of a superior who amazes him too greatly, the inferior has no other resource than that of handing in his resignation.

**The rift in authority**: Up to this point, everything above him had been, to his gaze, merely a smooth, limpid and simple surface; there was nothing incomprehensible, nothing obscure. Authority was a plane surface; there was no fall in it, no dizziness in its presence. Javert had never beheld the unknown except from below. Now Javert threw himself back, and he was suddenly terrified by this unprecedented apparition: a gulf on high. **Javert could not return Valjean to the Rue de l'Homme Armé. It was clear that that was what he ought to do. He could not.**

## Summer Year 8 Seasonal Observations
The road was all ruts and puddles after the thaw. The light went early, as it did that time of year. Rain threatened since morning but held off. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Clouds predicted rain wrongly. Wind came off water with salt and tar smell. Dogs barked at nothing. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps. **Coachman humbly represented to "monsieur l'Inspecteur" that Utrecht velvet of his carriage all spotted with blood of assassinated man and mire from assassin; added indemnity due; drew certificate book from pocket, begged inspector to have goodness to write "bit of attestation."** In Staveford: Rimor laughed at story nobody else found funny; Rimor watched clouds and predicted rain wrongly; Kassa remarked river up again; Ismira said it always was in spring; Ismira hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; Gadrek laughed at story nobody else found funny. In Ostcombe: Road all ruts and puddles after thaw; baker's boy late again, line at oven grew long; Lurald read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. **Price of salt scandal (Volan and Matho discussed).** **Luvie fell asleep in chair before fire had caught. Thizek argued with carter over price of sack of oats.**
